extracted.intended_audience: Executive Officers, department chairs, promotion & tenure committees, and faculty (tenure-track and Specialized Faculty) involved in evaluating instructional contributions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for systematic, fair evaluation of faculty instructional contributions (classroom and non-classroom) for annual review, third-year review, promotion, and reappointment—intended to guide department-level review processes and documentation. Emphasizes multiple measures (student surveys, peer review, self-assessment) and lists evidence types across five instructional dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and accessibility of expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any and all department, college, and/or university-level expectations, criteria, and procedures for the evaluation of teaching be clear and accessible to all faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from AAUP principles: departments should publicize specific processes for evaluation of instruction for each category of faculty employed; expectations must be transparent to support fair evaluation and faculty development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualized use of evaluation data
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurate and systematically collected data on faculty teaching be put into institutional context (as relevant to support, resources, and types of teaching done) in order to be assessed fairly and without unwarranted assumptions or conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICES and other measures should be interpreted in light of course characteristics, disciplinary norms, resources, and known biases; evaluation packets (e.g., promotion) should contextualize teaching effectiveness, particularly for courses commonly ranked low across instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple, complementary measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Differing measures of evaluation emphasize different aspects of the classroom experience and are thus each part of a fuller portrait of teaching effectiveness: student evaluation forms (perception), peer evaluations (observation), self-evaluation (reflection), and where applicable external review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No single measure should be sole determinant; faculty should have a primary (but not exclusive) role in evaluating their teaching; aggregate multiple sources to form assessment and development plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation as development and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of teaching is beneficial for both faculty development and instructional effectiveness, and distinguished teaching resulting from the evaluation of faculty should be recognized accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is not purely punitive; departments should use reviews to identify improvement opportunities and to recognize excellence (e.g., nominations for teaching awards, internal/external recognitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual evaluation requirements (tenure-track)
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of annual review, departments should ask that faculty write a brief overview of their contributions to teaching, including information about Q1 and Q2 scores on any ICES forms and any specific improvements or changes made to teaching during the year under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments should also provide opportunities for peer review of teaching in each of the six years of the probationary period leading up to tenure review; ICES forms should be included in annual reviews per Provost guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-year review requirements (tenure-track)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-year review must include ICES data for Questions 1 and 2 from all courses taught prior to the review, and should ideally include three or more peer evaluations summarized by the Executive Officer, as well as a self-assessment of teaching by the candidate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-year review summarizes prior annual reviews and indicates any difficulties in research or teaching; peer evaluations should be summarized by the EO in the review packet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion and tenure teaching documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The promotion and tenure packet must include a summary of all teaching evaluation items from the third-year review (and subsequent reviews), all ICES score information, and should contextualize teaching effectiveness; external letters of review regarding the candidate's research are also required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualization is especially important where courses are commonly ranked low by students; packet should clearly assess candidate's success as teacher and researcher and include teaching materials and summaries of peer/self-assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual evaluations and promotion for Specialized Faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Specialized Faculty should undergo annual evaluations (ICES forms, peer review) with particular attention to excellence in teaching as the primary criterion for reappointment; promotion procedures follow Provost Communications with unit-specific departmental procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reviews must be conducted per Provost Communication #25; units should maintain documents outlining departmental procedures for promoting Specialized Faculty (see Communication #26).

rubrics_metrics.name: ICES (student course evaluations) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: ICES forms should be distributed or made available electronically near the close of each semester; ICES scores are required for tenure and promotion files per Provost guidance and student written comments can provide valuable formative feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICES should be used iteratively to engage students in relation to instructors' goals; faculty may design alternative course surveys to augment ICES but must protect student identity/confidentiality and may work with CITL to design discipline-specific core questions (ICES FAQ and CITL resources referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty peer review of teaching (purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty peer review provides a contextual, professional perspective on how a faculty member's teaching succeeds in relation to pedagogical aims and disciplinary norms and should complement student surveys which can reproduce biases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is essential to form a fuller portrait of teaching, guard against bias in student evaluations, and support faculty development, awards, and formal review packets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer observation best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Best practices for peer review dictate specific procedures to ensure fairness, preparation, and usefulness of classroom observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required/Recommended practices include: (1) faculty choose course and date (within availability), (2) notify faculty at least one week prior and, if possible, provide specific questions, (3) peer has syllabus and brief sketch of class plan, (4) a written, dated, signed overview of the visit with suggestions provided in a reasonable time, (5) option for a follow-up conversation and action plan, (6) if department head/chair observes and is significantly negative, faculty have access to peers for a second review, (7) faculty should have reasonable choices of reviewers for formal observations. Links to sample rubrics and pre-observation forms (LAS Teaching Academy, College of ACES, AE3 instrument) provided for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of peer observations (pre-tenure and others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each pre-tenure faculty member should be observed multiple times before third-year review and before application for tenure and promotion to Associate Professor; Specialized Faculty and graduate student instructors should be observed on a regular cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations may be formal (part of annual/third-year/promotion reviews) or informal (mentoring); reviews serve both development and documentation purposes for reappointment, awards, and promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty self-assessment (purpose and design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-assessment is a mechanism for faculty to reflect on teaching, set pedagogical goals connected to student learning goals, and document instructional work in statements included in promotion/tenure packets or teaching portfolios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be flexible, designed around the faculty member's goals, can be periodic or course-specific, iterative in nature, and be a central part of annual review alongside peer reviews and ICES. Examples and templates referenced (e.g., Washington State University CTL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum — evidence of contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators for evaluating curriculum development and course content: syllabi with course goals and learning objectives; writing assignments, exams, and evaluation instruments; peer evaluations of course content; comparison of course materials across sections; importance of courses for departmental curriculum; development or significant modification of courses; revision/development of degree programs; content suitability for follow-on courses; grants and awards for course/curriculum development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these artifacts as evidence in review packets to show design, alignment with learning goals, curricular impact, and sustained curricular contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classroom Instruction — evidence of teaching effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators for classroom teaching: lesson plans, lecture slides, course websites; student course evaluations and written comments; multiple peer evaluations; incorporation of technology; development of new teaching techniques/materials (simulations, case studies); guest lectures; awards for instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and summarize multiple peer observations, ICES Q1/Q2 scores and comments, and artifacts demonstrating active and effective instruction; these items support annual reviews and promotion packets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra-classroom Instruction — evidence of mentoring and experiential teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators include direction of independent studies; direction of senior honors, master's, and doctoral theses; membership on graduate review/qualifying/dissertation committees; supervision of internships; presentations before student organizations; co-authorship with students; involving undergraduates in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document advising, mentorship, thesis supervision, internship supervision, and student research involvement as part of teaching contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration/Service related to teaching — evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators include student advisement and faculty advisor roles; service on instruction-related committees; service on education-related professional committees; editorial or reviewer roles for education journals/grants; leadership/presentations at education workshops; mentoring faculty/students; supervision of large multi-section courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture service activities that directly support instruction and student learning at department, college, campus, profession, and community levels as part of teaching evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) — evidence and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence includes authorship of textbooks; adoption of textbooks by others; grants related to scholarship of teaching; development of instructional technology/software; instruction-related publications, papers, and reports; participation in teaching seminars and improvement programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions to SoTL should be rewarded under teaching (not research) unless faculty are specifically hired for such duties; SoTL is not a substitute for discipline-based scholarship for most faculty and should be documented appropriately in teaching dossiers.
